column1: Pella/s0|Did he explain why you could not go?|Yes. He was worried about the road and did not want to hide that behind an excuse.|Do you still study the globe?|Yes, though I know it cannot show everything a traveller would notice.

Pella/s1|Would your father come too?|I would like that. It began as a journey we meant to make together.|Will you draw what you see?|Probably, after giving myself time to look without turning it into homework.
Pella/e0|Do you keep it at home?|Yes. I can spend longer studying it there.|Does it make you more eager to travel?|It does, provided I remember paint is only a beginning.

Pella/e1|Why not seek an adventure?|The journey itself will be new enough. I do not need danger to make it count.|What would you bring home?|My own memories, and perhaps a drawing that needs correcting less.

Pella/w0|What makes the roads frightening?|The creatures and the patrols. A royal claim of safety does not remove either worry.|Does studying places still help?|It gives me questions to ask when travel becomes possible.|Would you travel without preparation?|No. Wanting to see the coast is not a reason to ignore conditions.

Pella/w1|What will you arrange first?|A suitable route, provisions and company. A plan requires more than pointing at the coast.|Will your father be pleased?|I hope we can talk about making the journey together again.|Will your map change afterwards?|It should gain details I actually observed, marked separately from what I had only read.
Bess/s0|Were you worried nobody would come?|Terribly, until I worried where everyone would sit.|Why did people bring cups?|They knew I was starting with little and wanted the first night to work.

Bess/s1|Does a song settle a real quarrel?|No. It may calm the room enough for people to stop making it worse.|What if someone keeps causing trouble?|Then I ask them to stop, and to leave if necessary. The room belongs to other customers too.

Bess/e0|Why not use it for drinks anymore?|A chipped rim is no kindness to someone's mouth.|Do you measure all the supplies with it?|Only the dry goods it suits. Familiar equipment still needs a sensible purpose.

Bess/e1|Can a lively room still be comfortable?|Certainly. Comfortable does not mean everyone whispering.|What do you do if people shout over a newcomer?|Give them a chance to be heard without turning it into a performance.

Bess/h|Do you believe a frequent traveller more?|Only about things they can account for. Repetition of a journey does not certify every story.|What if nobody was actually there?|Then I call it a rumour and keep pouring.

Bess/w0|Do the soldiers question customers?|They listen and ask enough that everyone notices them listening.|Can you ask them to leave?|That is harder when they claim to represent the king.|What should keeping the peace mean here?|Stopping harm, not making a quiet conversation feel suspicious.

Bess/w1|Are people less guarded now?|Some. Others still pause when the door opens.|Does the noise bother you?|Ordinary argument is manageable. Fear was worse for the room.|Will you change the tavern rules?|People still pay, behave decently and mind the furniture. Liberation has not altered that.

Ronan/s0|Did you actually intend to make it that sharp?|No. Claiming I had was an attempt to rescue my pride.|How did the next batch improve?|Careful notes and better control of the process, instead of hoping confidence would help.

Ronan/s1|Why does that tree ripen later?|Its variety and growing conditions differ. I learned its season rather than judging it by the others.|Does waiting always give sweeter apples?|No. These apples have a known habit; waiting is not a recipe for every tree.
Ronan/e0|How do you know when they are ready?|Condition and taste, with the tree's usual season in mind.|Have you ever waited too long?|Long enough to learn that patience still includes checking.

Ronan/e1|Why does cleaning matter so much?|Dirty equipment can spoil the next batch, however good the fruit.|Would a song make it easier?|It might improve the mood. It will not remove the need to scrub.

Ronan/w0|Why stop pouring when the room quietens?|I want to hear whether someone needs help before carrying on as though nothing happened.|Do all uniforms cause that reaction?|Enough do that customers have learned to expect trouble.|Can you keep the mood cheerful?|Sometimes. I cannot pour away a reason people are frightened.

Ronan/w1|What are they arguing about?|Which cider is too sharp, which cup is too small. Fine, ordinary complaints.|Do you join the arguments?|When my cider is accused, naturally.|Why did you miss them?|Because nobody thought an opinion about a drink required looking over a shoulder.

Venn/s0|Why haven't you delivered it yet?|I have not located the intended recipient. I keep looking when a lead appears.|How do you know what it says?|I was asked to help establish where it belonged. I do not normally open the letters I carry.
Venn/s1|Why did she wait to ask?|She wanted someone she trusted with private news.|Did you read it to her?|When she asked. I remember how much a short, clear message could matter.

Venn/e0|Would you open an undeliverable letter?|Only with proper permission or a clear arrangement from the sender. Curiosity is not enough.|Do you ever meet the people waiting?|Sometimes. Their relief explains why a small parcel deserves care.

Venn/e1|What if they want someone else to read it?|Then I give them the letter. Helping does not make the choice mine.|Do you explain difficult wording?|If asked, while keeping clear which words are the writer's.
Venn/h|Why number the letters?|So a family could notice a missing one instead of assuming nobody had written.|Did carriers keep the bundles dry?|They tried. Weather and accidents still caused losses.

Venn/w0|Do families avoid important news?|They sometimes disguise names or soften what happened, fearing an unwanted reader.|Have soldiers opened letters?|People have reason to fear inspection. It changes how they write.|Can a carrier promise complete privacy?|I can promise care and honesty about the risks, not control every checkpoint.

Venn/w1|What invitations would you like to carry?|Visits, weddings, ordinary plans made without an explanation for an officer.|Will people write more openly immediately?|Some will. Others have practiced caution for years.|Will careful delivery still matter?|As much as ever. A hopeful letter still needs to arrive.

Hobb/s0|Did removing the legs solve it?|Yes, once we stopped trying to argue with the width of the door.|Would you do it differently now?|Measure first, dismantle what can be safely removed, and keep the fittings together.

Hobb/s1|Why stop at three legs?|The fourth needed better fitting. Saying I was researching sounded more impressive.|Will anyone test it before you finish?|Not if I can prevent it. An unfinished chair should not invite an unsuspecting sitter.

Hobb/e0|How will you check the joints?|Properly, before putting weight on it. I can ask someone better at the craft if needed.|Does the fourth leg match the others?|Close enough to fit, I hope. Hope will still need a measurement.

Hobb/e1|Would measuring first help?|Immensely. It also deprives everyone of a very energetic argument.|Who should give directions while carrying?|One person at a time, with the others allowed to say stop.

Hobb/w0|Do the royal men pay later?|Not reliably. The crown's account seems to lead away from Bess's purse.|Have you challenged them?|I have objected. They find my own tab an amusing distraction from theirs.|Will you pay what you owe?|Yes. Their bad behaviour is not a reason to cheat Bess myself.

Hobb/w1|Are you paying the tab off?|I intend to. Bess is admirably clear about whose account it remains.|Did you expect it to be cancelled?|Only for the pleasure of making the suggestion.|Would you help Bess instead?|If we agree what work counts toward it. I cannot appoint myself paid by being helpful.

Edric/s0|What spares did you leave behind?|The ones whose weight exceeded any realistic use I could explain.|What about food and water?|Necessary supplies stay. Travelling light is not travelling unprepared.

Edric/s1|Do you write down those quiet days?|Sometimes, briefly. I want to remember contentment as well as mishaps.|What makes an uneventful day worthwhile?|The company, the view, and arriving with enough strength to enjoy the evening.

Edric/e0|Was the confidence false?|Some of it. A heavy bag cannot prepare you for every problem.|Have you ever missed an item you left?|Yes. Then I reconsider that choice rather than repacking everything.

Edric/e1|Do you prefer travelling with company?|Good company, yes. Quiet need not mean being alone.|Would you call that a successful journey?|Certainly. Arriving safely and content is a perfectly respectable result.

Edric/w0|Why were workers afraid of a knock?|It might bring another demand or questions about something said in confidence.|Did anyone help those neighbours?|Often. Those small acts mattered more than the speeches promising care.|What would change your judgment of a ruler?|How people actually live under the decisions, not how those decisions are described.

Edric/w1|Whom should we remember?|The people who shared food, offered shelter and kept useful work going.|Should those people govern everything?|Not automatically. Kindness is worth remembering without assigning someone every task.|How can we preserve the examples?|Tell the stories accurately and practice the same care when another neighbour needs it.

Dorr/s0|Does Bess mind you sleeping here?|She tells me when I am occupying space she needs. I listen.|Do you miss unloading wagons?|Not the coldest mornings. I miss some of the people more than the loads.

Dorr/s1|Could you have gone back to sleep in the dream?|Apparently my imagination respects a finished shift better than real life does.|Were all the jobs truly finished?|For that marvelous moment, yes. Do not examine it too closely.

Dorr/e0|Do you always wake in time?|No. My reputation is doing some of the work in that claim.|Would a bed be more comfortable?|Undoubtedly. This is a nap, not an argument for new sleeping arrangements.
Dorr/e1|What do you do when you wake early?|Remember I can stay put, then try to convince the rest of myself.|Would you return to that work?|Not merely because my body remembers the hour.

Dorr/w0|Would you rather rest now?|Yes. I can dislike a king after my head clears.|Is there anything you want to say briefly?|That a day's work should leave a person some life afterwards.|Should I come back another time?|For a long political discussion, please do.

Dorr/w1|Would you like some peace and quiet?|Very much. News this good deserves a comfortable chair.|What will you do after breakfast?|Decide after eating. I am experimenting with an unhurried morning.|Are you really done discussing him?|For today, if everyone permits me that enormous ambition.

Ser Anwen/s0|Who was being excluded?|People whose need had become inconvenient to the orders being issued.|Did they answer your question?|They treated the question as disobedience instead of producing the wording.
Ser Anwen/s1|Why repair the dummies yourself?|They needed mending and I knew how to stitch them.|Was learning to fight difficult?|Yes. Useful hands still need training for a new task.

Ser Anwen/e0|Do stable hands mind you checking?|I ask and work with them. Rank does not entitle me to interfere without understanding.|What do you look for?|Wear and damage that might fail under strain.

Ser Anwen/e1|Can an oath be too simple?|It needs enough clarity to guide action, without hiding exceptions in impressive language.|How would you explain yours?|Protect people. Then answer honestly for whether my actions did that.

Ser Anwen/w0|How do you recognise fearful silence?|By giving people a real chance to disagree and seeing what they finally say.|Can a soldier safely object?|Not always. That makes a commander's duty to listen more serious.|What should Halvard have heard?|The people harmed by his orders, without threatening them for describing it.

Ser Anwen/w1|How do we tell recruits from willing abusers?|Examine actions, choices and circumstances carefully. A uniform alone does not answer it.|Does fear excuse every action?|No. It helps explain circumstances; it cannot erase the harm.|What would a better beginning require?|Training, accountable leaders, and orders aimed at protecting people rather than frightening them.

Grusk/s0|Why not use a complete deck?|That was eventually the sensible conclusion. First I wanted Dain to appreciate his own rules.|Did Dain admit it was unfair?|In language that avoided the word admit.

Grusk/s1|Do you miss hauling barrels?|I miss being able to do it comfortably. My shoulder is clear about the distinction.|Could you teach someone else?|The safe methods, yes, without pretending I can still lift every demonstration.

Grusk/e0|Does the old injury still trouble you?|Enough that I respect it. Familiar work can tempt a person to forget.|Do you move furniture for Bess?|Only within what I can safely manage. I can help plan a move without lifting it all.

Grusk/e1|Have cards actually been missing?|Yes. Counting is a response to experience, not a mysterious insult.|Do you check the rules too?|Before we begin. Dain prefers discovery at a more profitable moment.

Grusk/w0|What would make the rules fair?|People knowing them in advance and having a real say in changing them.|Can a kingdom work like a card game?|Only as a comparison. The people affected cannot simply find another table as easily.|Why does leaving matter?|An agreement is hollow if refusal brings punishment.

Grusk/w1|Who should help set the new rules?|The people who must live under them, with the terms made clear.|How do we stop someone changing them secretly?|Keep decisions visible and make the person changing them answerable.|Will agreement be easy?|No. That is still better than discovering the cost only after paying it.
Fen/s0|Did counting help at first?|Yes. Once the steps were familiar, we could listen to the music instead.|Were you embarrassed about mistakes?|Until I realised my partner was busy making some too.

Fen/s1|Did you know the person who invited you?|Not well. The invitation let us begin with something easier than explaining my whole journey.|Did one dance change everything?|No. It was one good evening, followed by others.

Fen/e0|Can you tell just from shoulders?|Not certainly. I ask before deciding what help someone wants.|What do nervous dancers need?|A comfortable pace and permission to make a mistake without an audience judging it.
Fen/e1|Do you still notice the exits?|Yes, without letting that be the only thing I notice.|What makes a face familiar?|Small repeated conversations. Belonging is often built that way.

Fen/w0|Do the patrols stop the dancing?|Sometimes their presence is enough to quiet everyone.|Why keep dancing when they arrive?|When it is safe, I do not want every pleasant thing surrendered without a word.|Does Bess support that?|She wants a comfortable room. She also has to judge when a situation is turning dangerous.

Fen/w1|Will you invite more people to dance?|Anyone who wants to. An invitation should remain easy to decline.|Will Bess object to the floor wearing out?|Long before it happens, I expect.|What feels different while you dance?|I can attend to the partner and the tune instead of whoever just entered.

Senn/s0|Did the others all fold?|Eventually. They assigned a reason to my smile that had nothing to do with the cards.|Did your brother arrive?|Yes. That was the important good news, regardless of the hand.

Senn/s1|Do you set aside the breakfast money first?|Yes. Money I need should not become part of proving a point.|Does Dain try to keep you playing?|Naturally. His definition of a brave player benefits his purse.

Senn/e0|What do you do after losing?|Accept the result, check I am still within my limit, and leave when I should.|Is losing still annoying?|Of course. Annoyance does not entitle me to spoil the room.
Senn/e1|How small are the wagers?|Small enough that losing does not take necessities from tomorrow.|What if pride starts deciding?|That is a good time to stop, even if I dislike how stopping feels.

Senn/w0|Why compare his promises to a wager?|He makes other people bear the risk while claiming certainty.|Would you trust another promise from him?|I would ask what changed besides the wording.|Should people risk nothing at all?|No. They should understand and choose risks, especially when others may bear the cost.

Senn/w1|What uncertainty do you welcome?|Possibilities that were closed before, rather than guessing the next royal demand.|Are you still cautious?|Yes. Hope and keeping enough for breakfast get along well.|What would you do with a calmer future?|Enjoy ordinary evenings without assuming the next notice will spoil them.

Dain/s0|Can dirt really tell you a traveller's route?|Sometimes it offers a clue. It does not certify where someone has been.|Does Bess pay you for sweeping?|We agree how the work settles what I owe. She keeps a clearer account than I would prefer.

Dain/s1|Have you actually changed a rule midgame?|I have explained one inconveniently late. Grusk finds the distinction unpersuasive.|Will you agree the rules first now?|With everyone insisting so eloquently, I appear to have little choice.
Dain/e0|Does the dirt help you clean?|It tells me where the traffic has been. That is the reliable part.|Could you mistake one road's mud for another?|Very easily. A confident guess remains a guess.

Dain/e1|Could you write the rules down?|That suggestion has also been made, with an alarming amount of support.|Wouldn't clear rules prevent arguments?|Some arguments. I suspect Nyra would still discover things to say about my dealing.

Dain/w0|Would you really bar him?|I would rather not test how well a tavern rule holds against royal guards.|Are your own games honest?|More closely supervised than I would like. You may draw conclusions from that.|What makes his behaviour worse?|The people affected cannot walk away without fearing the consequences.

Dain/w1|Will you actually play fairly?|With Grusk counting everything, I shall display exemplary arithmetic.|Does Nyra agree with him?|Enthusiastically. I am surrounded by supporters of this reform.|Could an honest game still be fun?|I am being given every opportunity to discover that.

Rusk/s0|Did you stop when visibility worsened?|We slowed and stayed close until we could identify the route again.|Did the voice tell you the safe direction?|It kept us together. We still needed to confirm the path rather than follow a voice blindly.

Rusk/s1|Does your daughter know your route?|When I can send word. The address helps if someone else must contact her.|What if the paper gets wet?|I keep it wrapped and check it. A precaution is useful only if it survives the journey.
Rusk/e0|Who is meant to read the address?|Someone helping me if I cannot explain whom to contact.|Do you update it when she moves?|Yes. An old address can be as unhelpful as no address.

Rusk/e1|Did you tell him you had wanted quiet?|I admitted it over supper. He found enough amusement for another account of the journey.|Would you travel with him again?|Yes. I might ask for a little quiet while the weather was clear.

Rusk/w0|What makes a report trustworthy?|Where and when the traveller passed, what they actually encountered, and what they did not inspect.|Could an official report ever help?|Certainly, if current and based on evidence rather than a desired announcement.|Do conditions change quickly?|Weather and damage can. Yesterday's passage is useful news, not a guarantee.

Rusk/w1|What dangers remain?|Weather, poor footing and creatures on the roads. They have not read the news of his defeat.|Where would you seek fresh reports?|From people recently through the route, comparing more than one account if possible.|Does victory make travel easier at all?|It removes one serious source of danger. That matters without removing every other one.

Linnet/s0|Did the new words fit the old tune?|They were made to. Familiar music can make a new message easier to remember.|Did she keep humming afterwards?|Yes. The tune was part of her daily work long before the decree.

Linnet/s1|Do people tell you what they remember?|Sometimes afterwards. I do not ask everyone to explain a quiet expression.|Can the same tune feel sad and happy?|Very easily, depending on what someone brings to it.

Linnet/e0|Does the tune have a known origin?|Accounts differ. I distinguish what I know from the memories listeners attach to it.|Do you change how you play for each room?|A little, listening to the pace and mood without pretending to know everyone's thoughts.
Linnet/e1|Did you learn it by listening to her?|Yes. Repetition taught it before I thought of it as a lesson.|Do you hum while working too?|Sometimes, and suddenly I remember her hands kneading.

Linnet/h|How do words change between villages?|People adapt them for their work, names and celebrations.|Should one version replace the others?|Not merely because someone calls it the original. The variations have histories too.

Linnet/w0|Why does a tune keep older memories?|People learned it in homes and gatherings before hearing the new official words.|Can he forbid the melody too?|He can order it. He cannot ensure every person forgets it.|Do you still play the old tune?|With care for the people listening as well as myself.

Linnet/w1|Who remembers the older verses?|Families and singers who kept them privately. I ask rather than assuming my version is complete.|Will you keep the variations?|Yes, with their sources, instead of combining them into a falsely certain original.|Would you perform them again?|When people want to hear them. Preserving them should also let them be sung.

Puck/s0|Did Bess teach you patiently?|Patiently enough, with direct opinions about that unfortunate note.|Why practise behind the tavern?|I thought fewer people would hear my mistakes. The open windows disagreed.

Puck/s1|Why almost name someone famous?|I wanted the tune judged generously before anyone knew it was mine.|Were you glad you told the truth?|Yes. Recognising my own work would have become difficult after denying it.

Puck/e0|Can you practise too quietly?|If I stop learning the control the performance needs, yes. I choose a suitable time too.|Has that difficult part improved?|Enough that the neighbours no longer recognise only the mistake.
Puck/e1|Do people hum it back to you?|Sometimes. Hearing it in another voice is a peculiar pleasure.|Have you written another?|I keep trying. One recognised tune does not write the next one for me.

Puck/w0|How do you know which songs are forbidden?|Warnings and what other musicians have encountered. The uncertainty is part of the worry.|Does fear make playing harder?|It is difficult to think about a difficult passage while watching the door.|Would you rather play your own songs?|Sometimes, but inventing a tune does not stop someone inventing an objection.

Puck/w1|Are you still nervous performing?|Yes, about ordinary things such as losing the tune.|What will you play first?|Something I have practised properly and want people to hear.|Does a free audience mean an easy one?|No. They may dislike it openly, which is at least an honest response.
